claim: MoE training does not require expert parallelism to be useful: MegaBlocks trains MoE-XS, MoE-Small and MoE-Medium language models on a single A100 80GB GPU (batch 512 sequences, sequence length 1024, 10B tokens) and only uses 8-way expert model parallelism for the larger 8-GPU comparison.
stance_target: the implicit assumption that an MoE experiment on this box must use EP; a single-GPU or expert-replicated DP MoE run is a legitimate experiment
scope_conditions: A100 SXM4 80GB, CUDA 11.5, CUTLASS 2.5, mixed precision; vocabulary 51200, seq len 1024, head size 64
quoted_support: We trained all models on a single A100 GPU with a batch size of 512 sequences... We trained all models on 8 A100 SXM4 80GB GPUs using 8-way expert model parallelism for MoE layers and data parallelism for all other layers.

claim: Block-sparse MoE kernels that never drop tokens deliver up to 40% end-to-end training speedup over Tutel and 2.4x over Megatron-LM dense at equal validation loss, and the advantage grows with model size.
stance_target: whether MoE training efficiency is recoverable through kernel-level work rather than fabric-level work
scope_conditions: 8x A100 SXM4 80GB; decoder-only LMs on The Pile; 64-expert top-1 MoE layers
quoted_support: Our approach never drops tokens and maps efficiently to modern hardware, enabling end-to-end training speedups of up to 40% over MoEs trained with the state-of-the-art Tutel library and 2.4x over DNNs trained with the highly-optimized Megatron-LM framework.

claim: Padding-based MoE implementations waste memory as well as compute: Tutel's padding cut the maximum usable micro-batch by 2x, 4x and 8x relative to MegaBlocks for MoE-XS, MoE-Small and MoE-Medium respectively.
stance_target: the claim that MoE memory budgets depend heavily on the routing implementation, which matters when fitting MoE on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: 8x A100 80GB, capacity-factor padding vs block-sparse dropless
quoted_support: For these models, we observed this increase in memory usage reduced the maximum micro batch size that Tutel could use by 2x, 4x, and 8x compared to MegaBlocks for MoE-XS, MoE-Small, and MoE-Medium, respectively.

claim: Token dropping materially costs model quality: a capacity factor of 1 yields a 0.15 validation-loss reduction while avoiding drops yields 0.26, a 1.73x larger gain, at the price of more than doubling MoE-layer math.
stance_target: the quality-versus-memory tradeoff any MoE experiment on this box must declare
scope_conditions: Transformer-Small scale, 10B tokens, GPT-2 tokenizer, seq len 1024
quoted_support: While the MoE with capacity factor of 1 achieved a 0.15 reduction in validation loss, the MoE that avoided dropping tokens provided a reduction of 0.26, 1.73x larger than the gain of the former model... In this example, MoE-layer math operations increased by over 2x in order to avoid dropping tokens.

claim: Some MoEs require capacity factors as high as 11 to avoid dropping tokens, and the required factor can spike unpredictably during training, making capacity-factor tuning an expensive hyperparameter search.
stance_target: the claim that MoE experiments are hyperparameter-expensive, which matters when each run costs days on a slow box
scope_conditions: as reported by Hwang et al. (Tutel) and reproduced in MegaBlocks' motivation
quoted_support: Hwang et al. (2022) showed that some MoEs require capacity factors as high as 11 in order to avoid dropping tokens, and other models where the necessary capacity factor to avoid dropping tokens spiked unpredictably during training.

claim: MegaBlocks reformulates MoE computation as block-diagonal block-sparse matrix multiplication with variable-sized blocks, which relaxes the constraint that all experts receive the same number of tokens and have the same shape.
stance_target: whether dropless MoE is implementable without custom fabric support
scope_conditions: GPU block-sparse kernels; num_experts x capacity_factor padding removed
quoted_support: In order to relax these constraints, we can construct a block diagonal matrix with variable sized blocks made up of many smaller blocks. We can compute this matrix efficiently using block-sparse matrix multiplication.
